question: After a developer adds a /lint-report skill, it works when they run Claude Code themselves, but a teammate who pulled the latest commit reports the skill doesn't exist. The developer confirms the file was never staged in any commit. What is the most likely cause?
options: A) The skill was saved under .claude/commands/lint-report.md, which requires a separate enterprise license to be shared across teammates.
B) The skill was saved correctly, but skill availability only activates after the project's CI pipeline runs once successfully.
C) The skill was saved under ~/.claude/skills/lint-report/SKILL.md, which lives outside the repository and was never version-controlled.
D) The skill was saved under .claude/skills/lint-report/SKILL.md, but the teammate needs to restart their machine before new skills are detected.
correct_answers: C) The skill was saved under ~/.claude/skills/lint-report/SKILL.md, which lives outside the repository and was never version-controlled.
explanations: Incorrect. There is no enterprise licensing requirement for sharing a project-scoped skill; committing the .claude/skills/ directory to version control is what makes it available to teammates.
Incorrect. Skill availability is not gated behind a CI pipeline run.

Correct. The personal ~/.claude/skills/ directory lives outside the git repository, so a skill placed there is never staged, committed, or shared with anyone else who clones or pulls the project; only a skill committed under the project's .claude/skills/ directory reaches teammates.
Incorrect. Claude Code does not require a restart to detect a newly added skill, and this doesn't explain why the file was never staged in a commit to begin with.
